_meta.description: Historical attacks and CVEs used as REFERENCE MEMORY: surfaced as hints in Stage 9 and in the PoC report's 'similar historical attacks' section. Summary-level facts only; verify details before citing externally.
_meta.trust: reference (never treated as a SOC-confirmed case, never decides a verdict)

attacks.name: WannaCry ransomware worm
attacks.summary: Worm that scanned for exposed SMB (TCP 445) and spread using the EternalBlue exploit; encrypted files and demanded ransom.
attacks.lesson: Block SMB/NetBIOS at the perimeter; patch MS17-010; segment internal SMB.

attacks.name: BlueKeep RDP vulnerability
attacks.summary: Wormable pre-authentication RDP flaw; mass internet scanning followed disclosure and a cryptomining exploitation campaign was later reported.
attacks.lesson: Never expose RDP directly; require VPN/NLA and patch.

attacks.name: MSBlast / Blaster worm
attacks.summary: Worm exploiting the Windows DCOM RPC interface on TCP 135.

attacks.name: Mirai IoT botnet
attacks.summary: Botnet that scanned for Telnet/SSH and logged in with a short list of default credentials, then launched large DDoS attacks (e.g. against Dyn).
attacks.lesson: Remove default credentials; disable Telnet; rate-limit and lock out repeated failures.

attacks.name: Colonial Pipeline ransomware incident
attacks.summary: Reported intrusion through a compromised VPN account lacking multi-factor authentication, followed by ransomware deployment.
attacks.lesson: Enforce MFA on remote access; retire unused accounts; alert on login success after failures.

attacks.name: Heartland Payment Systems breach
attacks.summary: SQL injection against a web application was the reported initial foothold, later used to install sniffing malware on the payment network.
attacks.lesson: Parameterised queries, WAF rules for injection tautologies, and least-privilege database accounts.

attacks.name: TalkTalk customer-data breach
attacks.summary: SQL injection against legacy web pages exposed customer records.
attacks.lesson: Retire or patch legacy web assets; monitor for 500-error bursts on login endpoints.

attacks.name: MOVEit Transfer SQL injection campaign
attacks.summary: Zero-day SQL injection in a file-transfer web app exploited at scale for data theft.
attacks.lesson: Patch internet-facing file-transfer products immediately; hunt for web shells after injection indicators.

attacks.name: Equifax breach (Apache Struts)
attacks.summary: Remote code execution through a crafted request to a vulnerable Apache Struts application (injection-class web exploit).
attacks.lesson: Patch known-exploited web frameworks quickly; maintain an accurate asset inventory.

attacks.name: Samy worm (MySpace)
attacks.summary: Stored cross-site scripting worm that propagated through user profiles.
attacks.lesson: Context-aware output encoding and a strict Content-Security-Policy.

attacks.name: TweetDeck XSS worm
attacks.summary: A crafted tweet executed script in viewers' TweetDeck sessions and self-propagated.
attacks.lesson: Sanitise rendered user content; deploy CSP.

attacks.name: Emotet loader campaigns
attacks.summary: Long-running malware-as-a-service; documents/macros launched encoded PowerShell that downloaded further payloads.
attacks.lesson: Alert on PowerShell -EncodedCommand and script hosts spawned from user processes; block macro execution from the internet.

attacks.name: QakBot loader chains
attacks.summary: Banking trojan turned loader; delivery commonly used script hosts (VBScript/JScript) to fetch and run payloads.
attacks.lesson: Restrict wscript/cscript; alert on script hosts launching downloads.

attacks.name: SolarWinds SUNBURST
attacks.summary: Trojanised software update beaconed to attacker-controlled domains over HTTPS to receive tasking.
attacks.lesson: Egress filtering and DNS/URL reputation blocking limit the value of a backdoor.

attacks.name: Log4Shell
attacks.summary: Remote code execution via JNDI lookups in Log4j; vulnerable servers called out to attacker infrastructure to fetch payloads.
attacks.lesson: Unexpected outbound requests from servers to unknown domains are a strong exploitation signal.
